one_liner: Stockroom and inventory job for the Capitol Visitor Center gift shops: counting, ordering, and moving merchandise, packing online orders, and covering the sales floor.
fit_summary: The posting requires 52 weeks of specialized experience in warehousing, maintaining a stockroom, managing inventory and space allocation, and completing electronic inventory paperwork. Nothing on file shows Daniel has done that work, and consulting on emergency management does not equal it unless the IEM role included real supply, logistics, or property accountability tasks. Daniel's people skills and policy knowledge would help on the customer-service side, but they are not what screeners will qualify on.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring path: public); you must be a U.S. citizen, which Daniel is presumed to be.

You need at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05: warehousing and maintaining a stockroom, managing inventory including space allocation, and accurately completing electronic inventory paperwork.
You must be able to pass a drug test; the security clearance is listed as 'Other', so expect some background check.
You must meet all qualifications by the closing date, November 16, 2026.
strategy: First check honestly whether your IEM work, or any earlier retail, warehouse, or event job, included 12 months of hands-on inventory, supply, or stockroom duties; if not, this posting will likely screen you out.

If IEM involved disaster logistics, such as tracking commodities, staging supplies, maintaining equipment or property inventories, or using tracking databases, describe it in the posting's own terms: accountable property, reconcile, requisitions, space allocation.
Use the USAJOBS preview of the questionnaire, and rate yourself 'expert' only where your two-page resume shows specific inventory examples; HR checks your answers against your resume.
Keep the resume to two pages, with dates, hours per week, and title for each job, and put the specialized experience bullets at the top of the relevant job.
Apply well before 11:59 pm ET on November 16, 2026, and confirm all required documents are uploaded.

Since your real strengths are policy and public engagement, also watch for AOC/CVC Visitor Services jobs, congressional office jobs, and FEMA or Virginia VDEM emergency management roles, which fit you better.
resume_bullets: Tracked and reconciled [number] items of [supplies/equipment/commodities] using [system/spreadsheet], performing [weekly/monthly] counts and correcting discrepancies in electronic records.
Coordinated requisition and replenishment of [materials] for [project/event/disaster operation], maintaining stock at [levels] and organizing storage space in [location/warehouse].
Documented overages, shortages, and damaged items in [system], and prepared transfer and accountability records for [number] shipments.
interview_questions: Describe a time you found a discrepancy between a physical count and inventory records. How did you resolve it?
How would you organize a storeroom with limited space during a busy holiday season?
Tell us about handling a frustrated customer, either in person or about an online order.
What inventory or data-entry systems have you used, and how did you make sure your entries were accurate?
watch_outs: The specialized experience requirement is strict and inventory-specific; without it, you will be rated ineligible.
You must work Saturdays and holidays, the job is physical (lifting and transporting materials), and there is no telework.
Promotion potential tops out at GS-06, so this is a limited ladder for your policy-oriented career goals.
The commute from Manassas to Capitol Hill is long; factor in VRE schedules, since VRE does not run on weekends or most holidays.
